cells.tense: Right now you're the one tending it, and your hands are steady.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, at the pace it actually grows.
cells.place: In the long stretch of standing with something while it takes its time.
cells.ask: Offer the next bit of care one beat slower than you could — and let what comes back be that the giving stops costing you.
cells.core: Right now you're the one tending it, and your hands are steady. Not gripping it and not gone from it — you hold what's fragile without squeezing the life out of it, and you keep at it past the point where most people would have gotten impatient. That steadiness is why things around you actually get to grow, and why the people you hold feel held instead of managed.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what's growing, and your hands are steady.

cells.tense: Somewhere up ahead of you the thing's already in trouble and you're getting there first, already bracing for it.
cells.verb: Holding so hard it stops letting anything breathe.
cells.place: At the edge of a future you can't write in, carrying weight nobody's handed you yet.
cells.ask: Let one worry stay undecided for a day — enough light for the next step, no more — and notice that what comes back is a picture built from what you've actually lived, not from what you fear.
cells.core: Somewhere up ahead of you the thing's already in trouble and you're getting there first, already bracing for it. You call it caring, and it started as caring, but the holding has gone tight — you carry what isn't yours, you give past your own edge, and somewhere in it you start keeping score of what it costs you. The weight you're spending all that strength on hasn't even arrived yet, and the tightness is what's keeping it from growing.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying weight nobody's handed you yet.

cells.tense: Somewhere back there you stopped having anything to give and called it being fine on your own.
cells.verb: Standing available to nothing, and calling that independent.
cells.place: Still at a door that's already behind you, holding form where nothing's coming through it.
cells.ask: Let one thing you actually want pull you toward it — following what draws you rather than what you think ought to — and let what comes back be light that's yours because what you tended got to finish.
cells.core: Somewhere back there you stopped having anything to give and called it being fine on your own. Nothing's growing because you stopped offering anything to grow — you've gone hard to keep going, and independence is the story you tell about the distance. The capacity to hold is still there; what stopped is the reach toward anything worth holding for.
cells.sheetLine: You have care to give and you've stopped giving it.

cells.tense: Right now you're the one everyone comes to, and you'd tell me that's just what you do.
cells.verb: Tending everyone's growth while yours goes unfed.
cells.place: In a role you never signed up for, holding a room you didn't say you'd hold.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do for someone else out of care and call it what it is — and let what comes back be one load set down, not something taken from you.
cells.core: Right now you're the one everyone comes to, and you'd tell me that's just what you do. They lean on you and you're there — but you didn't pick this, and you're running on empty while you hold everyone else up. The care is real and it's doing real work; the person giving it just never got to say whether it was hers to give.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding everyone up and calling it just what you do.
